### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **138** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 85e29b8858b55a6dab39f8b7f004290743a25da8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0002894704ae3ffeac0bc2aa0dc1e50b77b5f2f9` — the merge of head `c222ab563b65319ac713f766ad58b088ba46890a` into base `85e29b8858b55a6dab39f8b7f004290743a25da8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0002894704ae3ffeac0bc2aa0dc1e50b77b5f2f9 && git checkout 0002894704ae3ffeac0bc2aa0dc1e50b77b5f2f9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 85e29b8858b55a6dab39f8b7f004290743a25da8 c222ab563b65319ac713f766ad58b088ba46890a && git checkout -B drift-repro 85e29b8858b55a6dab39f8b7f004290743a25da8 && git merge --no-ff c222ab563b65319ac713f766ad58b088ba46890a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 85e29b8858b55a6dab39f8b7f004290743a25da8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

'page'` plus `resolveOverlayWidth(navigation)`. The gantt `.describe()` records the renderer's `{ mode: 'drawer' }` absent-key default, which matches :1960.

**Writer census — SOUND; no measured writer refused.** Re-derived read-only at the pin: every distinct authored `navigation:` literal in a file naming one of the three types is `{ mode }` with one of the seven modes, some with `size`, `openNewTab`, `preventNavigation` or the deprecated `width`, all of which the schema declares. The non-parsing values are refusal probes (`'anything'` parity probe, `{ mode: 'sideways' }` / `{ mode: 'not-a-mode' }` expected-issue probes, a bare `'drawer'` under `@ts-expect-error`) or prose in docblocks. My file counts differ from the dev's 88 / 98 / 59 (a broader substring matcher finds 168 / 153 / 91), which changes nothing: the conclusion is on values, and it holds. objectstack at the head: the only `navigation:` co-mentions outside `packages/spec/src` are CHANGELOG prose and this PR's own changeset — 0 writers on the three rows, as reported.

**2. The enumeration pin — RIGHT, with one recorded blind spot.** §1 fails on an unlisted `z.unknown()` (`census()` keys not in `LEDGER`) and on a stale ledger line (`LEDGER` keys not in `census()`); the size-equality control makes an empty walk impossible to pass. The dev's ablation (object-map `navigation` reverted with no ledger line → 8 failed, §1 names exactly that member; blob-proven restore) is consistent with that construction. The walk descends optional / nullable / default / prefault / readonly / catch / nonoptional wrappers, pipes on the input side, lazies, arrays, records, union arms, intersections, object shapes and catchalls, and §3 lights each position. The reasons, each checked against the source: **slot (7)** — §2 checks them against `pageComponentSlotPositions()` (`component.zod.ts:6941`); **runner (16)** — the action rows' `params`, `bodyExtra`, `bodyShape`, `operation`, `patch`, `toast`, `resultDialog`, `onSuccess` on `action:button` / `action:icon`; at the pin `action-button.tsx:181-298` forwards each into the runner's `ActionDef`, the row's docblock (:3098-3104) records that posture, each `.describe()` says "forwarded to the runner" and §2 checks the phrase — exactly the class triage's direction keeps as `z.unknown()`; **records (18)**, **shared (35)**, **any-value (1)** (`data-list.tsx:68`, `toText`), **open-bag (1)** (`pagination` is a `z.looseObject`), **no-reader (1)** (`placeholders.tsx:109-113` omits `ai:chat_window` on purpose; no registration anywhere at the pin, and app-shell's palette excludes it) — all honest. **Staged (27) + held (1):** 16 of the cited readers were resolved at the pin (`ObjectMetricWidget.tsx:250 / :254 / :265 / :267`, `ObjectForm.tsx:961, :1312-1313`, `ModalForm.tsx:854`, `ObjectGrid.tsx:2158, :4763, :4799-4815`, `KanbanBoardCore.tsx:95, :114`, `ObjectCalendar.tsx:296-297`, `ObjectGantt.tsx:2497`, `ObjectTimeline.tsx:551, :587`, `action-group.tsx:303`, `action-menu.tsx:339`); each is a real read of the named member. No `staged` or `runner` line hides a member this stage owed under triage's direction: the claim's size rule says census first, build the first group, then return a staging proposal before building past it, and the first group is the card's own named reach — the three `navigation` rows typed, kanban held under the caveat. Blind spot, not a defect: the predicate is `def.type === 'unknown'` only, so a future `z.any()` member would pass unlisted; `component.zod.ts` carries 0 `z.any()` today and the card's direction names `z.unknown()`.

**3. Staging under the claim's size rule — SOUND; `Part of #21464` — RIGHT.** The precedent spent 1,167 added lines on 7 members, about 140 non-generated lines per member; 28 × 140 ≈ 3,900 is a fair projection and more than one reviewable PR. The claim's own rule ("the dev stops after the census and returns a staging proposal before building past the first group") is followed to the letter. The Part-of gate is green and the card stays open for the stages.

**4. The held item, object-kanban `conditionalFormatting` — RIGHT.** `ListViewSchema.conditionalFormatting` (`view.zod.ts:2819-2834`) is a strict `{ condition, style }` with aliases and a `color` guidance. objectui at the pin authors both other dialects in its own kanban fixtures (`plugin-kanban/src/__tests__/ObjectKanban.structuredMembersReachTheirSinks-8313.test.tsx:459-485`: `{ field, operator, value, backgroundColor }` and `{ condition, backgroundColor }`) and asserts both on its `ObjectKanbanSchema` (`types/src/__tests__/kanban-conditional-formatting.test.ts:25-52`); `KanbanImpl.tsx:179` evaluates them through the shared evaluator. The by-reference narrowing would therefore refuse a measured writer, and triage's caveat says report, not ship silently — which the pin's `held-for-decision` line and the report do. The precedent could ship the grid's narrowing because its census found no writer of either dialect; the kanban census does. Observation: the kanban row's `.describe()` ('Card conditional formatting rules') carries no hint of the hold, so the recorded reason lives in the pin alone — acceptable under the card's "listed with its recorded reason".

**5. The retirement kit — three of four RIGHT, one STALE.**

- Step-18 rationale fragment, order 64: unique in `STEP18_RATIONALE` (the duplicated orders 56 / 60 / 62 are pre-existing on `main`, not this PR's); the tracker citation in its text follows the file's convention (88 such citations), and `check:doc-authoring` is green. RIGHT.
- Generated registry region: byte-identical to the entry file, leading comment included, as the generator emits the precedent's. RIGHT.
- **Regenerated references page `content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx`: STALE against `main` — the failed gate.** Timeline from the trees: the dev merged `main` at `100c394f6f` (merge commit `58b235eba2`, 23:32Z) and regenerated; `fd96a8473d` (#21478, "one shared def renders one optionality face on every reference page") landed on `main` at 23:35Z — three minutes later — changing `packages/spec/scripts/lib/format-type.ts` so the Type-cell shape summary marks every defaulted member with `?`; the final commit `d3431deed3` (23:41Z) and the PR (00:37Z) followed with no second merge. On `main@6f17d1d364` every typed `navigation` Type cell reads `{ mode?: …; preventNavigation?: boolean; openNewTab?: boolean; size?: …; … }`, and `fd96a8473d` itself rewrote the grid / calendar / timeline rows from the old face to that one. The PR's three NEW rows for `ObjectGanttProps`, `ObjectMapProps` and `ObjectTreeProps` (head `component.mdx` :587, :954, :1189) carry the superseded face `{ mode: …; preventNavigation: boolean; openNewTab: boolean; size: …; … }`. On the merge commit the generator renders them with `?` and the sync check reds — the one row of AGENTS.md §10 / §11 ("never trust git's textual merge of a generated file") this head trips. The dev's STALE TREE note was honest when written: it named `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` against `origin/main` `5555047117`, which predates `fd96a8473d`. The remedy is mechanical and seat-side: merge `origin/main` (now `85e29b8858`), `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` and `check:generated --fix`, commit, push; the new head then needs its own record.

### ② Semver level

**RIGHT, and identical in shape to the precedent.** `.changeset/21464-component-props-navigation-typed.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, a `feat(spec)!:` title, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, the **BREAKING** banner with the launch-window `minor` convention sentence, the adr-0087 `registered` marker naming the one id `ui-object-map-gantt-tree-navigation-typed` (the precedent named three because it also carried a D2 conversion and a retired-key entry; this PR registers no conversion, with the reason recorded in the D3 entry), a FROM → TO table, and a measured "Who is affected" section. `Check Changeset` is green on this head, and the dev's `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` readings agree with the text.
